caption: Loan Servicing
vo: Booking a loan is the easy part. The real work is looking after it, every day, until it's repaid. Let's see how Genesis CRM helps.

caption: The loan book is a daily snapshot from the loan system (LMS)
vo: Every day, the loan book arrives as a snapshot from the LMS. The LMS stays the system of record. The CRM services from it.

caption: Sign in as Rajiv Doorgakant — Manager, Loans & Fixed Income
vo: We start with Rajiv Doorgakant, the loans manager. He reviews the book every morning.

caption: Lending ▸ Loan Servicing ▸ Loan Book: one row per loan account
vo: One row per loan account. Rate, days in arrears, the arrears bucket, maturity and LTV, all on one screen.

caption: Show only the accounts in arrears: search for “In arrears”
vo: But Rajiv only cares about trouble first. So he searches for in arrears, and sorts by days in arrears.

caption: Open LMS-100202 — a home loan 45 days in arrears
vo: Here's one. A home loan, forty-five days behind.

caption: Outstanding principal and the current rate: PLR minus the product margin
vo: The outstanding principal, and the current rate, which is PLR minus the product margin. Variable loans like this follow every PLR change.

caption: Monthly instalment and the next due date
vo: The monthly instalment and the next due date. Three days before each one, the borrower gets an SMS, in their own language.

caption: Days and amount in arrears, the bucket, maturity and the current LTV
vo: And the arrears detail. Here's the thing: the moment an account slips into arrears, its RM gets a collections follow-up automatically.

caption: ALCO has decided to cut the Genesis PLR by 25 bps, from 6.825% to 6.575%
vo: Now, some news. ALCO has decided to cut the Genesis PLR by twenty-five basis points, from six point eight two five to six point five seven five percent. Every variable-rate borrower needs to be told.

caption: Sign in as Sophie Lagesse — Loans Executive
vo: That job starts with Sophie Lagesse, our loans executive. She prepares the campaign.

caption: Loan Servicing ▸ PLR Change ▸ New: old rate, new rate, effective date
vo: Old rate, new rate, and the date it takes effect.

caption: “Approved by” stays empty — the campaign is only a draft
vo: Notice she leaves approved by empty. This is a draft, and nobody has signed it off yet.

caption: The campaign starts in Draft
vo: It starts in Draft, then Approved, Notices generated, and Distributed.

caption: Try to move it to Approved…
vo: So, can she approve it herself…

caption: Blocked: the person who drafted a campaign cannot approve it
vo: No. Whoever drafts a campaign can't approve it. That's four eyes: the loans manager signs it off and records the ALCO approval.

caption: Meanwhile, the RM works the early-warning follow-ups
vo: While that waits, let's go back to arrears. The daily arrears check gave every account in arrears a call to make.

caption: Sign in as Bruno Chan — Relationship Manager (Corporate)
vo: Bruno Chan is the relationship manager who owns those borrowers.

caption: Loan Servicing ▸ Collections: arrears bucket, action, date and outcome
vo: Collections shows the bucket, the action, the date and the outcome. And the history stays right here: earlier calls, demand letters, disputes.

caption: Log the call on LMS-100202: the borrower promises to pay
vo: Bruno calls the borrower on that home loan, and she promises to pay, recorded on the follow-up the CRM already opened.

caption: Save without the promised date…
Refused: a promise to pay needs the amount and the date
vo: Refused. A promise to pay needs an amount and a date. Otherwise, who knows when to chase it?

caption: Add the date she gave and save again
vo: So Bruno adds her date.

caption: The promise is written on the loan account
vo: And now it's on the loan account itself. Promise to pay by, for everyone to see.

caption: LMS-08810: 95 days, no contact, and the demand letter is disputed
vo: This next one is harder. Ninety-five days, no contact, and the demand letter is disputed. Time to escalate, so Bruno logs a new action.

caption: Escalated — the loans manager is alerted at once
vo: The loans manager is alerted straight away. In the ninety-plus bucket, the case now takes the legal recovery route.

caption: The loans manager signs the PLR change off
vo: Now back to that PLR campaign. Drafted by the executive, it now needs the manager.

caption: Sign in as Rajiv Doorgakant — Manager, Loans & Fixed Income
vo: So we're back with Rajiv, and this time he's here to approve the PLR change.

caption: His notifications: the escalation from collections is already there
vo: And look, Bruno's escalation is already waiting in his notifications.

caption: Record who approved it — here the ALCO meeting he chaired
vo: He records who approved it. In this case, the ALCO meeting he chaired.

caption: Now move it to Approved
vo: Move it to Approved, and this time it goes through.

caption: Approving changes no rate by itself
vo: To be clear, approving changes no rate. The PLR, the website rate, and new loan pricing only move when the new rate is entered in Masters.

caption: The CRM now writes a notice for every variable-rate borrower
vo: What approval does do is this. The CRM writes a notice for every variable-rate borrower, same balance and term, new rate, new instalment.

caption: Done: the campaign moved itself to Notices generated
vo: And it's done. The campaign moved itself to Notices generated, counted them, and told the loans manager.

caption: Open Loan Servicing ▸ PLR Notices
PLR Notices: one per loan — borrower, new rate, change in instalment
vo: One notice per loan, with the borrower, the new rate and the change in instalment. Fixed-rate and settled loans are left out.

caption: Open the notice for LMS-08821
vo: Let's open one.

caption: Old and new rate, old and new instalment
vo: Old and new rate, old and new instalment, side by side. Notice the loan keeps its own margin. Only the PLR part of the rate moves, which is exactly what the borrower expects.

caption: The personalised letter was generated and filed on the notice
vo: The personalised letter is already written and filed on the Docs tab, ready to email, print or post.

caption: Rate and instalment before and after the effective date
vo: The letter shows the rate and instalment before and after the effective date. And the term of the loan doesn't change.

caption: Notices checked: move the campaign to Distributed
vo: Notices checked, so Rajiv moves the campaign to Distributed. Every borrower gets an email, in English or French.

caption: Distributed: the emails go out and each notice is marked Sent
vo: The emails go out, and each notice is marked Sent. Nobody sends them by hand.

caption: Every notice is now Sent, with the date
vo: Every notice now says Sent, with the date. And if an email bounces, it's flagged for a call or a letter by post.

caption: The email is on the notice's Activity timeline
vo: It's on the timeline too. What the borrower was told, and when.

caption: Dashboard ▸ Loan Book
vo: Finally, the Loan Book dashboard. Outstanding by product, arrears buckets, LTV bands, the share that's PLR-linked, and how collections are going. It's the morning review on one page.

caption: The promise to pay just logged is in the collections outcomes
vo: Bruno's promise to pay is already counted. Click any chart to see the accounts behind it.

caption: Loan Servicing
vo: So that's loan servicing. A rate change from draft to every borrower's inbox, and arrears worked before they grow. The LMS keeps the books, the CRM looks after the borrowers.
